angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 197,579 km at 62.35 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 16.0392 +/- 0.0256 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 62.35 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.284 +/- 0.041 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-91 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract): 197,579 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.292 +/- 0.058 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-91 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3622 +/- 104 K from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-91 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-91 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-91.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.997, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
